emily_ml: quick thought — our current onboarding runs heavy bench + full evals on every new artifact. want to propose a stratified smoke layer between ingest and full bench to catch obvious incompat and perf regressions faster

raj_platform: curious — what do you mean by stratified? multiple quick checks instead of 1 big run?

emily_ml: exactly. idea is 3 lightweight strata: 1) metadata & artifact shape checks (onnx/ggml headers, dtype, param counts) 2) micro-bench smoke (1-3 requests, check kv cache hot path, memory allocs) 3) quality quick-check (small eval set, deterministic prompts)

tess_research: i like that. makes the admission pipeline more incremental. we should ensure the quick quality checks use the same eval prompts that catch hallucination/class-breakers for that family.

ben_runtime: runtime compatibility smoke is important — the micro-bench should exercise attention kernel paths and quantization codepaths. something like:
```
# pseudo workload for smoke
input = random_prompt(seed=42, len=64)
for model_variant in variants:
  run_infer(input, max_new_tokens=32)
  assert no OOM, latency < 300ms, kv_hits >= threshold
```
That will catch missing ops and big regressions quickly.

emily_ml: ^exactly. also propose we add a model "admit score" that is vector of pass/fail per stratum + quick heuristic for fallback model mapping if micro-bench fails but artifact checks pass. e.g., tag as `soft-admit` and route to lower-capacity variant automatically.

raj_platform: operationally, we need the admit metadata to travel with the model artifact in registry. versioned keys like `admit:v1` with fields: strata:[meta,bench,qual], results, link->bench run id. keep schema minimal.

onboard-bot: CI: stratified-smoke job queued for artifact a1b2c3 — estimated runtime 2m

tess_research: one more tradeoff — false positives from flaky micro-bench. recommend we run each micro-bench twice on separate hosts and require failure on both to block. also keep a moving baseline of latencies per model family.

ben_runtime: agree. we should also record kernel fallback traces when we see slowdowns so runtime team can triage (and we can auto-suggest quantization switches).

emily_ml: next steps i propose: (1) draft tiny RFC for strata definitions + admit schema (2) prototype micro-bench harness in `onboard-smoke/` (3) wire admit metadata into model-registry publish hook. i'll draft this week, pinging @raj_platform and @ben_runtime for infra/runtime parts. :+1:

raj_platform: 👍 i'll allocate infra ticket and estimate. prefer to surface admit flags in console early so teams can see why a model is `soft-admit`.

ben_runtime: i'll add the kernel trace bit and a small perf harness. happy to pair on prototype.

emily_ml: thanks all — goal is to reduce expensive full-bench runs by ~30% for low-risk artifacts and speed up feedback for model authors. will share RFC link when ready.
